learning_objective: 🏃‍♂️ Understand the mechanics of movement, from the sliding microscopic filaments inside your muscles to the complex skeletal system and joints!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Movement is any change in posture (like blinking or moving your hands). Locomotion is a voluntary movement that results in a change of location (walking, running, swimming). All locomotion is movement, but not all movement is locomotion.

Skeletal muscles are made of muscle bundles (fascicles), which contain muscle fibers (cells). Inside the fibers are myofibrils, which have repeating structural units called sarcomeres. The sarcomere contains thin (Actin) and thick (Myosin) filaments.

How do muscles contract? With the help of ATP (energy) and Calcium ions, the thick Myosin heads grab onto the thin Actin filaments and pull them towards the center of the sarcomere. The filaments 'slide' past each other, shortening the muscle.

Divided into two parts: The Axial skeleton (80 bones) includes the skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum. The Appendicular skeleton (126 bones) includes the limbs (arms and legs) and their supporting girdles (shoulder and pelvic).

Joints are points of contact between bones. Fibrous joints don't move at all (like skull sutures). Cartilaginous joints allow slight movement (between vertebrae). Synovial joints allow free movement (like the hinge joint in the knee or ball-and-socket in the shoulder).

fun_activity.title: 🦾 The Sliding Hand Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Hold your hands in front of you with fingers spread open. Interlock the fingers of your left hand with the fingers of your right hand. Now, slide them together so your hands close in on each other. This is exactly how Actin and Myosin filaments slide past each other to contract your muscles!

exam_tips: 📌 Calcium ions (Ca++) play a critical role in muscle contraction by binding to Troponin, which unmasks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filament.
📌 Understand the Rib cage: True ribs (1-7, attached to sternum), False ribs (8-10, attached to 7th rib), and Floating ribs (11-12, not attached anteriorly at all).
📌 Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue and paralysis.
quick_recap: ⭐ The central part of the thick filament (myosin) not overlapped by thin filaments (actin) is called the 'H zone'.
⭐ The red colored, oxygen-storing pigment present in muscle fibers is called Myoglobin.
⭐ Gout is the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.
